author: Jae-wook Lee, **Hyun-Sik Jeon**, Yong-Soo Choi*
title: Using a LiDAR sensor for autonomous driving in a low-end environment
short_description: Developed a real-time static obstacle avoidance system using ROI-based LiDAR processing and Pure-Pursuit on a low-spec Windows platform.
abstract:
• **Problem**: As autonomous driving technology advances, the importance of sensors increases. However, most research relies on high-spec CPUs and extensive datasets for object recognition using LiDAR.
• **Solution**: This study focuses on avoiding small static obstacles (traffic cones) in a **low-spec environment** (Windows 10, Python 3.9.6) to improve accessibility. We utilized the **WeGo ERP42 platform** and **Velodyne VLP-42 LiDAR**. By applying **ROI processing** to remove unnecessary coordinates and using **Voxel Grid Filter** algorithm, we optimized data processing speed and recognized traffic cones as unified objects. A **linear regression** model was used to generate a driving path based on the slopes of the left and right cones, followed by **Pure-pursuit** and **Ackermann steering** control.
• **Result**: The implemented algorithm successfully verified real-time obstacle recognition and avoidance steering between traffic cones, confirming that autonomous driving can be implemented even in low-spec environments to enhance accessibility.
